detail.title: Real Value Added: Incidence and Comovement
detail.abstract: I develop a theory of real value-added incidence for arbitrary firm clusters: sectors, regions, countries, supply chains, or nongeographic groups of firms. In a general-equilibrium economy with input-output linkages, heterogeneous households, and rent-generating wedges, I show that cluster real-value-added growth decomposes into a factor-supply component and total factor productivity (TFP), with TFP further split into technology, competitiveness, and distributional reallocation. The sufficient statistics generalize Domar weights from aggregate productivity accounting to incidence accounting: they measure how firm shocks, factor supplies, household expenditure, firm revenue, markups, ownership, and network structure affect the real value added of a given cluster. I implement the decomposition for U.S. sectors. Aggregate TFP is shaped by a small set of sectoral contributors and drags: computers and electronics and oil and gas extraction are major positive contributors, while farms, construction, and housing are major drags. Sectoral TFP comovement is distinct from level contribution: large Domar sectors and upstream cost-central sectors tend to move against the rest of the economy, while sectors with concentrated downstream customer bases are less synchronized with the aggregate. Around the Great Recession, the TFP measure reveals pre-crisis expansion without efficiency gains and crisis-period downsizing with rising measured efficiency, patterns not visible in revenue data; it also identifies selective medium-run scarring.

title: Marketing Self-deception
affiliations: University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business and University of Cambridge - Judge Business School

detail.title: Marketing Self-deception
detail.abstract: A consumer may distort available information in ways that support a favorable belief. Such self-deceptive tendencies can be aided by the marketer through an implicit claim that eases the consumer's cost in distorting external information. This research explores the marketer's role in delivering self-deceptive benefits to the consumer. Our goal is to understand the market conditions under which self-deception arises in equilibrium. We further explore how the firm's ability to deliver self-deceptive benefits affects its incentive for innovations that materially improve its product. Our findings provoke the idea that marketplace deception has a demand-side component and can be welfare enhancing.

title: Decision Integrity Index: A Behavioral Methodology for Evaluating Agentic AI Systems

detail.title: Decision Integrity Index: A Behavioral Methodology for Evaluating Agentic AI Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is developing the Decision Integrity Index as part of an independent research and applied framework. No vendor-specific ranking is presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This working paper presents a conceptual and methodological framework and does not report a study involving human participants, patients, personal data, or empirical vendor data.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this working paper.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly deployed not only to generate information but to shape, structure, and accelerate human decisions. Existing approaches to AI evaluation typically focus on technical performance, safety, transparency, or regulatory compliance. However, they rarely assess whether an AI system preserves or weakens the user's ability to make reflective, accountable, and non-manipulated decisions. This working paper proposes the Decision Integrity Index, a behavioral methodology for evaluating agentic AI systems from the perspective of human decision-making quality. Drawing on behavioral economics, research on heuristics and cognitive biases, human-AI interaction studies, and emerging AI governance frameworks, the paper introduces the concept of decision integrity as a complementary dimension of AI system assessment. The proposed methodology combines a technical readiness layer, behavioral safeguard indicators, a Human Reliance Calibration Index (HRCI), and a practical human oversight quality assessment. It is designed to identify how AI systems may amplify automation bias, framing effects, overreliance, false certainty, confirmation bias, and loss of human agency. The paper argues that AI governance should move beyond formal compliance and include measurable behavioral safeguards. The proposed methodology is intended for further empirical validation and practical application in organizational AI procurement, public-sector AI evaluation, and responsible deployment of agentic AI systems.

title: Economic Scenario Generators as Stochastic Investment Models: A Comprehensive Review
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana., Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana.,  and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana.

detail.title: Economic Scenario Generators as Stochastic Investment Models: A Comprehensive Review
detail.abstract: Economic Scenario Generators (ESGs) have become essential tools in actuarial science and financial risk management, enabling institutions to simulate multiple, internally consistent paths of future economic variables for asset-liability management, regulatory capital calculation, and strategic decision making. The expansion of the literature into a range of modeling paradigms creates the need for a systematic synthesis. This paper presents a comprehensive review of ESG development viewed as stochastic investment models, based on a systematic literature review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) structure. The paper is organized into four main contributions. First, it establishes the conceptual foundations of ESGs, defining their purpose and contrasting stochastic simulation with deterministic forecasting. Then, it provides a structured classification of principal modeling approaches, analyzing each approach's theoretical foundations, strengths, and limitations. It also synthesizes the evidence on calibration practices and validation methodologies, drawing on the limitations documented in the reviewed literature to identify persistent challenges including parameter instability, structural breaks, and the complexity-parsimony trade-off. Finally, it examines ESG applications across diverse geographic contexts, with particular attention to emerging and data-constrained markets, extracting lessons for practitioners operating outside mature market environments. By identifying several open research challenges, this paper aims to support both academic researchers seeking to advance the field and practitioners navigating the trade-offs inherent in model selection and implementation. This paper also highlights that while significant progress has been made since the 1980s, the evolution of ESG methodology remains an active and essential endeavor as the demands on these models continue to expand.

title: The Continuing Lack of Widespread Adoption of Electric Vehicles
affiliations: Purdue University School of Civil and Construction Engineering

detail.title: The Continuing Lack of Widespread Adoption of Electric Vehicles
detail.abstract: The need to address growing environmental concerns and advancements in electric charging technology continue to motivate the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). However, EV market share remains limited. This study identifies the factors that continue to impede rapid adoption of electric vehicles. In a discussion, the paper argues that comprehension and duly accounting for these factors is critical if policymakers, manufacturers, and stakeholders are to realize their goals of accelerating EV adoption and achieving sustainability goals. The paper concludes that addressing these issues thoroughly will be essential to enhance EV adoption.

title: Pakistan in Global Value Chains: Comparative Evidence on Participation, Upgrading, and Structural Constraints

detail.title: Pakistan in Global Value Chains: Comparative Evidence on Participation, Upgrading, and Structural Constraints

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Publicly available data was used.
declarations.funderStatement: It is completely self funded by Author.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates Pakistan's participation in global value chains (GVCs) relative to five comparable South and Southeast Asian economies over 1990-2018, using the Koopman, Wang, and Wei (2014) decomposition of trade in value added. We decompose GVC participation into backward and forward linkages for Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Indonesia, and apply fixed-effects panel regression to test whether Pakistan exhibits a distinct trajectory. Three findings stand out. (1) Pakistan's compound annual growth rate of GVC participation decelerated from 14.81% in 2000-2010 to 2.19% in 2010-2018, an 85% decline; however, this deceleration is regional rather than country-specific-all six economies experienced comparable post-2010 slowdowns consistent with global trade headwinds. (2) Pakistan's forward ratio has drifted from 0.77 in 1990 to 0.94 in 2018, indicating persistent concentration in final-stage export activities with limited backward integration into imported intermediates. Panel regressions with country fixed effects yield a positive withincountry association between GVC scale and the backward ratio (β = 0.254, p < 0.001), but a Pakistan×Post-2010 interaction term is not statistically significant in the full sample and flips sign across subsamples, indicating that Pakistan's low-backward-ratio structure was established well before 2010 and is not a post-crisis phenomenon. (3) Crosscountry structural indicators are consistent with binding constraints on upgrading: Pakistan's Economic Complexity Index (-0.233) and Logistics Performance Index (2.59) are the lowest in the sample, and its export concentration (HHI = 0.118) exceeds all peers except Bangladesh and Cambodia. These results reframe Pakistan's GVC challenge: not a recent deterioration, but a persistent structural position whose resolution requires targeted intervention in logistics capacity, export complexity, and sectoral diversification rather than aggregate participation-boosting measures.

title: Cognitive Entropy: Interpretive Dispersion in Complex Informational Environments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cognitive Entropy: Interpretive Dispersion in Complex Informational Environments
detail.abstract: AbstractMany cognitive frameworks implicitly assume that interpretation tends toward sufficient stabilization over time, even under conditions of uncertainty, ambiguity, and incomplete information. This paper argues that some contemporary informational environments may increasingly sustain competing interpretations without durable convergence.Cognitive Entropy (CE), in this context, refers to the degree of interpretive dispersion within informational environments. Rather than describing pathology, cognitive dysfunction, or informational quantity alone, CE concerns conditions in which multiple structurally plausible interpretations remain simultaneously viable without stabilizing around a single dominant interpretive state.Contemporary informational environments are increasingly characterized by simultaneity, continuous updating, fragmentation, recursive reinterpretation, and algorithmic mediation. Such environments may sustain interpretive multiplicity across extended periods of time, complicating processes of stabilization, consensus formation, and meaning construction. Under these conditions, interpretations may become increasingly dispersed, even in the absence of individual cognitive deficits or extreme informational ambiguity.The discussion is conceptual rather than empirical. The aim is not to replace existing cognitive theories, but to provide a framework for examining how informational environments influence the relationship between information, interpretation, and stabilization. The paper concludes by outlining implications for cognitive science, information studies, decision-making, and future research on cognition in increasingly complex informational environments.

title: Service Recovery Analysis in the Food Manufacturing Sector: A Study Using Large Language Models

detail.title: Service Recovery Analysis in the Food Manufacturing Sector: A Study Using Large Language Models

keywords: Natural language processing JEL classification: M31

detail.abstract: Effective complaint management in the food industry requires response strategies that integrate perceived justice principles to optimize consumer satisfaction. A gap exists in understanding which specific communicational elements in corporate responses generate greater effectiveness in service recovery. This research investigates whether corporate responses implementing high distributive, interactional, and procedural justice are positively associated with greater consumer satisfaction in food product complaints. Computational analysis using Large Language Models (LLMs) with zero-shot learning is employed to identify perceived justice elements in food manufacturers' responses recorded in SENACON (2020-2025). LLMs automatically quantify compensation and empathy, statistically correlating them with consumer satisfaction evaluations through hybrid validation combining expert human coding (n=300) with algorithmic analysis (n=5,465). Empirical findings challenge the central hypothesis, revealing practically null correlations between the binary presence of justice elements and consumer satisfaction (r=0.02 for distributive justice, r=0.06 for interactional justice). The research contributes to service recovery theory by demonstrating that traditional frameworks require significant adaptation for digital contexts, establishes methodological precedents for LLM analysis in business-consumer communication validation, and provides evidence that response quality and contextualization are more critical than the simple presence of empathetic or compensatory elements in food industry complaint management.

title: Source Independence Is a Measurable Property of Evidence

detail.title: Source Independence Is a Measurable Property of Evidence
detail.abstract: When several sources agree, that agreement is routinely treated as corroboration: in pharmacovigilance, concurring reports are counted; in ensemble and multi-model systems, the independence of the members is assumed; in evidence synthesis, k agreeing sources are read as k-fold support. None of these practices measures whether the agreeing sources are in fact independentwhether they are distinct observations or echoes of a single origin. I report that source independence is a measurable property of evidentiary provenance, and I establish four facts about it. First, it can be measured from provenance alone, without models, ground-truth labels, or the content of the sources. Second, it is irreducible to any single proxy-not shared institution, not a shared source flag, not a shared citation-which I show through a reproducible inversion: across four therapeutic areas, sources sharing a literature reference are consistently measured as more dependent than sources sharing a submitting organization, the reverse of the naive expectation. Third, it is domain-general, holding across medical imaging and pharmacovigilance. Fourth, it converts into an effective count of independent sources, making apparent corroboration auditable. Together these establish that the assumption-agreement is corroboration-is testable, and routinely false. The measurement is implemented in Verdict Weight; its internal mechanism is out of scope here.

title: Experienced Disadvantage, Belonging, and Career Intentions in Quantitative Coursework: A Pilot Study
affiliations: Harz University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Experienced Disadvantage, Belonging, and Career Intentions in Quantitative Coursework: A Pilot Study
detail.abstract: How do students experience disadvantage in the quantitative and statistical components of business and economics degrees, and is that experience linked to their career intentions? We examine this in a predominantly female sample drawn from business, economic-psychology, and related programmes, a setting that departs from the male-dominated STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) on which most of the relevant literature rests. The contribution is twofold. Substantively, we give a first descriptive account of experienced disadvantage, entry prerequisites, study difficulties, and career intentions in this under-studied setting. Methodologically, we develop and pilot a questionnaire for these constructs, since no single validated German instrument covers experienced disadvantage, sense of belonging, and statistics self-efficacy jointly within the length of a classroom survey. With this instrument (N = 120), we describe the sample, estimate the prevalence and structure of experienced disadvantage, examine the difficulties students report, and explore how three psychological constructs (general self-efficacy, confidence in presenting statistical results, and sense of belonging) relate to the intention to enter a quantitative occupational field. Experienced disadvantage was rare and strongly floor-distributed; where reported, it most often concerned having one's competence questioned and was most frequently attributed to gender. General self-efficacy and sense of belonging did not differ by gender, yet women reported markedly lower confidence in presenting statistical results (Cohen's d = 0.75). Career intention was associated with domain-specific self-efficacy and with belonging, but not with general self-efficacy. The most frequently reported difficulties, gaps in prior knowledge and time burden, point to concrete levers for teaching and student support. All inferential analyses are exploratory and generate hypotheses for a confirmatory follow-up survey. We close with the measurement implications and the revisions they suggest for the instrument.

title: Methods for Analyzing Recreation Demand using Onsite Survey Data
affiliations: UGA Ag & Applied Economics and University of Georgia - Department of Agricultural & Applied Economics

detail.title: Methods for Analyzing Recreation Demand using Onsite Survey Data
detail.abstract: Onsite surveys are affected by avidity bias such that users who visit the site are more likely to be sampled. The effect of avidity bias causes uncorrected models of visitation to overestimate the number of visits of the average user of the site. Similarly, time spent on site affects the probability of being sampled. This paper reviews and extends the count data models that have been proposed to model onsite visitation data. We show that the negative binomial model may not be estimable when the onsite sample variance is large relative to its mean. Also, a bivariate count data model is developed to account jointly for both avidity and length-of-stay bias. Analysis of data on visits to Cape Hatteras National Seashore underscores the critical importance of model choice and specification in analyzing on-site survey data.

title: Vital Links, Divided Gains: How China's Transportation Boom Impacted Healthcare
affiliations: Singapore Management University, Singapore Management University - School of Economics,  and Peking University

detail.title: Vital Links, Divided Gains: How China's Transportation Boom Impacted Healthcare
detail.abstract: We study the impact of transportation infrastructure on healthcare access and health outcomes. Using administrative data on over 600,000 hospitalizations for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases (CCVD) in Sichuan, China, we show that patients travel from low-medical-resource to high-medicalresource cities, but travel time imposes substantial barriers, especially for low-income patients. We develop and structurally estimate a dynamic spatial model in which individuals choose treatment locations by weighing the expected effectiveness of care against travel and financial costs. Counterfactual simulations indicate that, holding medical resources fixed at the 2010 level, improvements in the national transport network between 2010 and 2018 would reduce CCVD mortality by approximately 10,000 cases per year. While geographic disparities in health outcomes narrowed, gains accrued disproportionately to high-income patients.

title: Modeling Ghana's Gdp: A Comparative Probability Distribution Approach
affiliations: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana., Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana - Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana - Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science,  and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana.

detail.title: Modeling Ghana's Gdp: A Comparative Probability Distribution Approach
detail.abstract: This study compares candidate probability distributions for modeling Ghana's annual gross domestic product (GDP) using data from 1960-2023. The Cullen and Frey Graph was employed to plot the square of skewness and kurtosis to determine the family of distributions the data follows. The data were determined to be positively skewed, and the likely distributions were Gamma, Exponential, Weibull, and Lognormal. Further statistical tests, such as the KL Divergence test, Goodness of fit, and information criteria, were used to confirm the likelihood of the distributions. The lognormal distribution emerged as the best fit for Ghana's GDP. Hence, the GDP of Ghana is best modeled by the lognormal distribution.

title: Uneven Cities, Uneven Finance:Climate Funds, Municipal Capacity, and the Urban Poor

detail.title: Uneven Cities, Uneven Finance:Climate Funds, Municipal Capacity, and the Urban Poor
detail.abstract: Despite a global increase in urban climate finance, the urban poor in the Global South continue to face acute deficits in climate-resilient water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. This paper investigates why climate finance fails to reach its intended beneficiaries by centering municipal public finance systems as the critical intermediary. Drawing on a multi-city empirical study across Dhaka, Khulna, and Rangpur in Bangladesh-a country at the frontline of climate change and rapid urbanisation-the paper examines how climate finance flows interact with weak fiscal decentralisation, fragmented intergovernmental transfers, and constrained municipal borrowing authority. Using 24 in-depth interviews conducted in urban informal settlements, combined with municipal finance analysis and an assessment of household service access data, the study finds that municipal fiscal capacity-not funding volume alone-determines whether climate finance reaches climate-vulnerable urban populations. Critically, climate-induced migration intensifies urban service deficits, creating compounding pressures on already fragile municipal financial systems. The paper contributes to the literature on climate finance governance and urban service delivery by surfacing the missing link between national-level finance architecture and local service outcomes. It concludes with targeted policy recommendations for strengthening municipal finance systems as a prerequisite for equitable climate adaptation.

title: Public Education in Greece: Insights from the Data
affiliations: and Yale School of Management

detail.title: Public Education in Greece: Insights from the Data

declarations.ethicsApproval: This project has been reviewed by IRB at Yale University (clearance number: 2000040434).

detail.abstract: Using newly linked administrative records on the universe of public-school students and their university applications and admissions from 2015 to 2025, this paper provides a data-driven portrait of Greek public education, documenting students' trajectories from secondary school to higher education, and what shapes student achievement. We find that average student performance has remained broadly stable over the past decade, with the exception of a post-pandemic decline in History. Learning gaps emerge early and remain persistent throughout secondary school. Girls consistently outperform boys across subjects, particularly in Modern Greek Language, and are  overrepresented among top-performing students in the national examinations. Furthermore, we study how schools, teachers, and classroom composition relate to student achievement. We find that the estimated variation in student learning growth  reflects both teacher composition and the broader institutional environment. Teachers assigned across fewer distinct subjects are associated with stronger student performance. Classroom sorting, as generated by alphabetical assignment, has heterogeneous effects and appears to benefit lower-achieving students while potentially reducing learning growth for higher-achieving ones. Finally, we study how students navigate the transition to higher education, and to what extent their choices are aligned with growing occupations in the labor market. We find that demand is highly concentrated in a small set of programs, reapplicants often revise their choices substantially, and placement into programs linked to growing occupations in the labor market varies significantly with exam performance and gender. Programs directly "universitified" after the 2018 reform saw increased demand and higher-scoring applicants. More broadly, the paper provides an empirical foundation to help inform future education policy discussions in Greece.

title: ESG Disclosure and the Cyclicality of Firm Growth
affiliations: University of Southampton - Southampton Business School

detail.title: ESG Disclosure and the Cyclicality of Firm Growth
detail.abstract: Exploiting adoptions of ESG reporting mandates across countries, we find that firms' asset growth becomes less cyclical following adoption. The effect is driven by lower asset growth and risky investment (R&D and acquisitions) during periods of strong GDP growth. The reduction is stronger among constrained firms, firms facing greater product obsolescence, and firms with shorter-term or less ESG-oriented institutional investors. ESG mandates also strengthen the response of productivity, profitability, and firm value to GDP growth. Overall, our evidence suggests that ESG disclosure affects the timing of firm growth over the business cycle through easing financing constraints and attracting ESG-oriented investors.

title:
Estimating the Distance to Consensus Instability: 
Latent Anchors and Mean Feedback in Inflation Expectations.

detail.title:
Estimating the Distance to Consensus Instability: 
Latent Anchors and Mean Feedback in Inflation Expectations.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: The author gratefully acknowledges the support of the DS4h Scholarship for fundings and support.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an econometric implementation of the Consensus-Instability Theorem (CIT) model and applies it to household and professional inflation expectations. Beliefs are represented as the sum of a slow latent anchor and a transitory discrepancy; the discrepancy mean-reverts, responds to cross-sectional mean feedback κ, and is reset when it exits a tolerance region. The associated fragility margin ∆ h = 1-κΦ h (0) measures the distance between a stable unimodal belief distribution and a regime in which feedback can generate bimodality. Under explicit measurement and reset-separability conditions,We derive identification results for the cross-horizon loading, discrepancy mean reversion, and mean-feedback parameter. The cleanest structural estimator of κ is an individual-transition IV estimator using external news; a news-free SMM estimator is developed as a model-conditional fallback.Wealso establish Hadamard differentiability of the ratio and IV functionals, obtain panel-bootstrap validity for that pipeline, and derive a Marriott-Pope small-T correction for the mean-reversion estimator. Monte Carlo exercises with 100 replications per design point show that the SMM estimator is approximately unbiased over the explored central grid. The news-free feedback estimates are small and positive: κSCE = 0.032 and κSPF = 0.048, with approximate standard errors of 0.014 and 0.018. These estimates place both panels well inside the stable region of the calibrated CIT model. The empirical contribution is therefore to estimate distance to instability, not to claim that inflation expectations are currently near a polarization threshold.

title: Hospital Inpatient DRG Billing Anomaly Detection and Risk Stratification: A Reproducible Composite Risk Score Methodology Applied to the CMS Medicare Inpatient Public Use Files, Fiscal Years 2019 through 2023

detail.abstract: Medicare Fee for Service improper payments reached $31.70 billion in Fiscal Year 2024, with hospital inpatient DRG severity coding contributing materially to documented federal program integrity concerns. This paper introduces a reproducible composite risk score methodology for detecting anomalous Major Complications and Comorbidities coding patterns in Medicare inpatient billing data. The methodology integrates five engineered features (Severity Mix Index, Payment Ratio, High Value DRG Concentration, MCC Volatility, Geographic Mismatch) into a weighted statistical risk layer, combined with an Isolation Forest machine learning layer for multivariate anomaly detection. Applied to 2,675 general acute care hospitals across 27,269,086 Medicare inpatient discharges in Fiscal Years 2019 through 2023, the system identifies 134 facilities (5.0 percent of the universe) demonstrating statistically anomalous patterns. Hospital specific weighted payment differentials computed from MS DRG Fiscal Year 2025 Table 5 relative weights yield directly observed excess billing of $75.7 million, with a bootstrap 95 percent confidence interval of $52.1 million to $103.2 million across 1,000 resamples. Temporal holdout validation training on Fiscal Years 2019 through 2022 and scoring on Fiscal Year 2023 produces 99.25 percent coverage of train flagged hospitals in the holdout year. All source data, code, persisted result files, and the interactive dashboard are publicly available under an open source license. The methodology is presented as anomaly detection and risk stratification, not supervised fraud classification, and flagged hospitals warrant investigative review by appropriate program integrity authorities.

title: Information Design in Selection Markets: A Bounding Result
affiliations: Leipzig University, , , Imperial College Business School and University of London, Imperial College of Science, Technology and Medicine - Department of Economics

detail.title: Information Design in Selection Markets: A Bounding Result
detail.abstract: We consider optimal information design in general quasilinear monopoly selection markets with finite types. We show how the analysis of a collection of two-type markets, each consisting of the highest willingness-to-pay type and one other type, can be used to derive a uniform bound on the welfare in markets with an arbitrary distribution of types. Whenever there are sufficiently many of the highest valuation types in the market, optimal information design can be used to achieve this bound. In canonical insurance market applications (with sufficiently many high cost types) we use our bounding result to show that any Pareto optimal segmentation has a striking feature: all types (other than the highest-cost type, who buys full insurance) purchase an insurance contract featuring the same deductible.

title: OCT-DCAFNet: A Dual-Coding Network with Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for OCT-Based Wind Turbine Blade Crack Segmentation
affiliations: North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University, North China Electric Power University and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: OCT-DCAFNet: A Dual-Coding Network with Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for OCT-Based Wind Turbine Blade Crack Segmentation
detail.abstract: Detecting wind turbine blade cracks in OCT images is crucial to wind power generation safety. However, it is often difficult for existing methods to detect the crack shape in the case of low image contrast, high noise and complex crack shape. This paper proposes a dual-coding network called OCT-DCAFNet, which uses auxiliary features to segment the OCT image cracks of wind turbine blades. We have verified the performance of the network on the OctCrack dataset. The OctCrack dataset uses porcelain cracks as a structural agent because their morphology is similar to that of leaf composite cracks. OCT-DCAFNet contains three independent parallel encoders. A CNN branch processes fine local texture details; a Transformer branch captures global context information; a RetinaNet ResNet50 branch provides target detection prior information to enhance feature representation. Each branch observes the crack image from a different perspective. The two modules integrate the information of these branches. The Transformer Channel Fusion (TCF) module exchanges channel information and applies spatial adaptive fusion to enhance feature complementarity. The adaptive two-way fusion module (ABFM) adopts the two-way cross-attention mechanism and deep separable convolution for further optimization. On the OctCrack dataset, the accuracy rate of OCT-DCAFNet reached 96.60%, the recall rate reached 96.24%, the F1 value reached 96.42%, and the IoU reached 93.09%. These data show that the network can reliably detect cracks under the surface in the actual industrial non-destructive testing environment.

title: Anomaly Detection and Risk Stratification for Medicare Durable Medical Equipment Billing Patterns

detail.title: Anomaly Detection and Risk Stratification for Medicare Durable Medical Equipment Billing Patterns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.

detail.abstract: This paper describes an unsupervised anomaly detection and risk stratification system applied to the universe of active Medicare Durable Medical Equipment (DME) suppliers. The work responds to a direct recommendation from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (audit report A 09 21 03019, May 2024) calling on the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to use predictive data analysis to identify emerging fraud schemes related to durable medical equipment. Using publicly available CMS supplier data spanning calendar years 2021 to 2023 (198,621 supplier year records, 44,918 active 2023 suppliers, 1,454,474 supplier and HCPCS service combinations) and the HHS OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (81,914 records), the methodology combines a weighted statistical layer (six z scored features with documented weights) with a machine learning Isolation Forest layer (eight features, contamination 0.02, n_estimators 100, random_state 42) at a 60 percent and 40 percent combination weighting. The system flags 2,246 suppliers (the top 5 percent by combined risk score), corresponding to $3.57 billion in directly observed above state median peer baseline excess billing (95 percent bootstrap confidence interval $2.98B to $4.22B, 1,000 iterations). A coverage adjusted national projection yields $7.18 billion. Validation rests on six independent procedures: bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation feature importance, temporal holdout (training on 2021 and 2022 data and evaluating on 2023, mean lift 7.93x, median lift 22.98x), honest OIG LEIE concordance, DOJ prosecution cross referencing, and OIG fraud typology pattern alignment. All artifacts including the analytical notebook, persisted result files, and interactive dashboard are publicly accessible under an MIT license to support replication and independent audit.

title: Low Birthweight and Child Achievement: Does Pre-K Compensate?

detail.title: Low Birthweight and Child Achievement: Does Pre-K Compensate?
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether pre-kindergarten (pre-K) attendance mediates the relationship between low birthweight and children's academic achievement in elementary school. Using the Early Childhood Longitudinal Study, Kindergarten Class of 2010-11 (ECLS-K:2011), a nationally representative sample that tracks children from kindergarten through fifth grade, I estimate a mediation model that combines OLS with heteroskedasticity-based IVs, following Lewbel (2012, 2018). The results confirm that low birthweight exerts a persistent, negative direct effect on standardized reading and math test scores throughout elementary school, with larger penalties for mathematics. The direct effect ranges from approximately-0.21 standard deviations in reading to-0.27 in math, and OLS estimates are systematically downward-biased in absolute value relative to the IV estimates. The estimated indirect effect operating through pre-K participation is consistently small and statistically insignificant, indicating that pre-K does not substantially mediate the birthweight-achievement relationship at the national level. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that the direct effect is substantially larger among low-income families, with IV estimates approaching-0.41 standard deviations, while high-income families show no statistically significant direct effect. Among lowincome households, the indirect effect through pre-K is positive, though imprecisely estimated. These findings suggest that the cognitive consequences of low birthweight are concentrated among disadvantaged children, and that targeted, high-quality early interventions-rather than broadly available pre-K programs-may be necessary to offset them.

title: Hassan, Anomaly Detection in Medicare Part D Opioid Prescribing

detail.title: Hassan, Anomaly Detection in Medicare Part D Opioid Prescribing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses only publicly available, de-identified CMS administrative data and does not involve human subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: Background. The HHS Office of Inspector General has identified opioid prescribing anomalies as a Medicare program integrity priority. Existing federal capability for prospective identification of statistical billing outliers among Medicare Part D opioid prescribers is limited and fragmented. Methods. We construct a reproducible anomaly detection and risk stratification framework on the CMS Medicare Part D Prescriber by Provider public use file for calendar year 2023, encompassing 1,380,665 prescribers. After analytical universe filtering and explicit clinical exclusions for oncology and palliative specialties, the modeling universe comprises 1,025,487 prescribers across 191 specialties and 61 jurisdictions. We engineer six per prescriber risk indicator features, compute a peer state plus specialty weighted z-score statistical risk layer, train an Isolation Forest machine learning anomaly detector at contamination 0.05 with random seed 42 on a standardized eight feature matrix, and combine both layers into a 0 to 100 anomaly score with the top 5 percent flagged for investigative prioritization. We validate findings with six pillars: bootstrap confidence intervals (1,000 iterations), permutation feature importance, temporal holdout validation against 2019 through 2022 training pool with 2023 holdout, OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities concordance, DOJ defendant cross reference, and OIG controlled substance fraud typology alignment. Results. The framework identifies 51,275 flagged prescribers (5.0 percent of the modeling universe), with directly observed sample excess of $1.16B above peer state plus specialty median prescribing. Bootstrap 95 percent confidence interval is $1.14B to $1.18B, with relative standard deviation 0.78 percent. Coverage adjusted projected national excess is $4.22B using a 27.5 percent Medicare opioid prescription share multiplier sourced from CDC and SAMHSA data. Method concordance between Isolation Forest and combined score is 92.0 percent. Temporal holdout coverage from 2019 through 2021 training pool to 2023 holdout is 70.5 percent for prescribers flagged in two or more training years. OIG LEIE direct NPI concordance is 29 matches. Conclusions. The framework provides an audit grade methodology for prospective Medicare Part D opioid anomaly detection that is fully reproducible from public federal sources. Results are robust under bootstrap resampling and demonstrate substantial temporal persistence across years. The framework is suitable for adoption by federal program integrity agencies for investigative prioritization, with explicit acknowledgment that anomaly scores are not fraud probabilities and that individual review by appropriate authorities is required before any inference.

detail.abstract: This paper develops and validates an unsupervised anomaly detection framework for Medicare telehealth billing across the post COVID era. Using the CMS Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners by Provider and Service Public Use File for calendar year 2023 (9.66 million row level records), we construct an analytical universe of 46,900 unique providers who billed any code in a 27 code telehealth HCPCS basket. We engineer nine per provider features including Payment per Beneficiary, Services per Beneficiary, HCPCS Diversity, and Audio Only Share. A Combined Risk Score integrates a documented statistical layer (weighted absolute z scores) and an Isolation Forest machine learning layer (contamination 0.02, 100 estimators, random seed 42) at 60 percent statistical and 40 percent ML weights. Providers above the 95th percentile of the Combined Risk Score (2,346 providers, 5 percent of the universe) are flagged. The flagged set accounts for $161.7 million in sample excess billing measured as Payment per Beneficiary above state median multiplied by beneficiary count. Bootstrap resampling at 1,000 iterations yields a 95 percent confidence interval of $145.5M to $179.2M. Sensitivity analysis confirms the headline finding is robust across alternative peer benchmarks ($128.0M to $164.0M range). Coverage adjustment using the CMS TMEDTREND Public File scales the sample to a national projection of $557.5 million, with no recovery rate multiplier. Validation includes permutation feature importance (Audio Only Share leads at 17.5 percent); temporal holdout where 79.9 percent of providers flagged in the 2021 plus 2022 training pool reappear in the 2023 holdout with mean Payment per Beneficiary 3.35 times the population mean; OIG LEIE concordance showing 5 direct NPI matches in the flagged set, a 7.1 fold enrichment over the baseline universe rate; DOJ defendant cross reference returning zero matches as expected. All code, data file hashes, and persisted result files are publicly available. The framework emphasizes the distinction between anomaly detection and supervised fraud classification, explicitly avoiding categorical performance claims that cannot be defended without labeled ground truth.

title: Bayesian inference for 3D activity reconstruction combining X-ray Computed Tomography and Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning
affiliations: Belgian Nuclear Research Centre SCK CEN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Ghent University and Ghent University

detail.title: Bayesian inference for 3D activity reconstruction combining X-ray Computed Tomography and Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the application of a Bayesian variational framework for 3D activity reconstruction in 220-liter radioactive waste drums. The method combines Angular Segmented Gamma Scanning measurements and attenuation information derived from X-ray Computed Tomography. Computations are made tractable using stochastic variational inference  together with a multi-resolution spatial prior for the inferred activities. A model to convert CT-derived gray levels into linear attenuation coefficients (CT-to-LAC), is developed to estimate energy-dependent attenuation maps from CT images, allowing the construction of the forward model under experimental conditions. Tests were performed using both homogeneous and heterogeneous mock-ups, with both point and linear sources made of either $^{241}$Am or $^{152}$Eu. Results show that the approach recovers spatial activity distributions broadly consistent with known source locations. Regarding the total activity of the drum, for multi-peak isotopes such as $^{152}$Eu, the true total activity is recovered within the posterior distribution and the posterior mean is more accurate than the estimates obtained from conventional averaging. In contrast, for the $^{241}$Am isotope, the reconstructions remain limited by the combined effect of single gamma energy line non-identifiability  and the stronger sensitivity of the LAC calculation errors at lower energies. This work provides the first experimental validation of Bayesian 3D activity reconstruction from ASGS and CT measurements, for radiological waste characterization.

title: The Verifiable Responsible Agent Framework: Making AI Agents Liable For Their Mistakes

detail.title: The Verifiable Responsible Agent Framework: Making AI Agents Liable For Their Mistakes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is an independent researcher and has no financial or personal relationships that could influence the shape of this work. The article advances a normative legal proposal (the Verifiable Responsible Agent framework) and does not endorse any specific commercial product, vendor, or proprietary standard; where existing technologies are named (e.g. the Model Context Protocol), they are cited as examples.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was started during the ERA Fellowship which is funded by ERA Cambridge. Later it was developed independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
Autonomous AI agents now deal in stocks, currencies and commodities. They do it at a speed and volume that defeats human intermediation. Yet, when one of them causes loss, no liable subject stands behind it: a model is not a legal person, and the operator who deployed it is often too far removed to be held liable. This article argues that the missing subject can be supplied without resolving questions of machine consciousness. It proposes granting agents a limited legal capacity made conditional on attested architectural constraints and bonded to insurance at the moment of issuance. The effect is that the legal form and the technical guarantee cannot drift apart-because enforcement requires a subject. It develops this Verifiable Responsible Agent (VRA) framework focusing on the horizontal coordination problems of private commercial transactions. Drawing on functionalist jurisprudence, principal-agent theory, and comparative institutional analysis, the article distinguishes what is verifiable today (operational-safety and commercially-reasonable constraints) from the fiduciary properties that remain a research frontier. Through examination of implementation possibilities in Delaware (US), the United Kingdom, and the European Union, it argues that incremental legal innovation can establish foundations for broader standardisation of AI-agent recognition while maintaining meaningful human accountability. The framework's technical architecture, cryptographic attestation, formal verification methods, open tool-use protocols (e.g., the Model Context Protocol), and standardised agent-agent communication, provides concrete implementation pathways that balance operational autonomy with verifiable compliance.
In the process of creating this article AI tools (Anthropic's Claude) were used e.g. to design graphical assets and for research purposes.

title: Survival versus Scale: The Effects of Critical Access Hospital Designation
affiliations: Emory University - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Survival versus Scale: The Effects of Critical Access Hospital Designation
detail.abstract: The Critical Access Hospital (CAH) program, established under the Balanced Budget Act of 1997, provides cost-based Medicare reimbursement to small rural hospitals in exchange for limits on inpatient capacity and service scope. We estimate the effects of CAH designation on hospital finances, capacity, and organizational outcomes using a synthetic difference-in-differences design that exploits the staggered 1999--2002 rollout of state-level CAH availability. We find no evidence that CAH designation meaningfully improves operating margins, with net patient revenue and total operating expenses both declining by similar magnitudes, consistent with proportional financial contraction as hospitals downsize to meet eligibility requirements. The primary effect is a reduction in operational scale, with significant declines in total beds, obstetric capacity, and nursing staff. At the same time, CAH designation reduces hospital closures, with no meaningful effect on mergers. These results point to a ``survival versus scale'' tradeoff wherein designation-based subsidies preserve hospital presence, but primarily through continued operation at a smaller scale rather than by maintaining pre-designation capacity. Because converting hospitals shed more capacity than avoided closures preserve, the program may reduce aggregate rural inpatient capacity even as it keeps hospitals open.

title: Cross-City Comparison of Crime-Prediction Models: A Scale Confound in Aggregate Poisson Likelihood, with a Four-City Demonstration
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin

detail.title: Cross-City Comparison of Crime-Prediction Models: A Scale Confound in Aggregate Poisson Likelihood, with a Four-City Demonstration
detail.abstract:
Objectives: Aggregate event-weighted Poisson predictive log-likelihood (PLL) is widely reported when comparing count-prediction models across populations of differing density (e.g., crime prediction across cities). This paper asks whether the metric is fit for that purpose and proposes an alternative metric pair for cross-population evaluation. 

Methods: The paper documents, algebraically and empirically, that aggregate PLL is confounded by zero-rate composition: the per-event log-likelihood ceiling, max y log p(y | µ) ≈-1 2 log(2πµ), becomes more negative as the predicted mean grows, regardless of model quality. The confound is demonstrated on a four-city LightGBM crime-prediction pipeline (Boston, Leeds, Birmingham, London) using publicly available incident data at H3-resolution-9 monthly granularity, with 5-seed ensembling and per-(city, type) honest decomposition. 

Results: Three different cities take rank-1 under three metrics-Birmingham on aggregate PLL, Boston on nonzero_pll_mean, London on calibration_ratio-and no city holds rank across all three. Denser populations appear systematically worse on aggregate PLL even when their honest per-event predictive likelihood and calibration are comparable or better. Four configuration-specific gradient-space negative results are also reported; the divergence-detection diagnostic against which they were tested measures sparsity rather than predictive pathology. 

Conclusions: The paper proposes nonzero_pll_mean and calibration_ratio as the primary cross-population evaluation pair, with zero_rate as descriptive context. Implications for cross-city benchmarking of crime-prediction models are discussed.

detail.abstract: Background. Population ageing and the expansion of morbidity have intensified interest in geroprotective interventions-therapies targeting the biological mechanisms of ageing rather than individual diseases. Existing health technology assessment (HTA) frameworks were designed for disease-specific technologies and may be poorly suited to interventions, the benefits of which accrue across multiple conditions over decades. The extent to which HTA and economic evaluation methodologies have been adapted for this intervention class is unclear.

title: CARB Regulations and Zero-Emission Trucks: Implications for California Agriculture
affiliations: California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo and California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo

detail.title: CARB Regulations and Zero-Emission Trucks: Implications for California Agriculture
detail.abstract:
California's zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandates for commercial transportation present significant challenges for the state's containerized agricultural export sector, particularly for specialty crops like almonds, walnuts, and pistachios transported from the Central Valley to West Coast ports. Despite regulatory rollbacks at the federal level -- including Congressional votes to block CARB mandates and the withdrawal of EPA waiver requests -- California and its ports continue to advance ZEV adoption through independent 'tariff-like' authority and incentive programs. 

This study, utilizing public records, industry data, and previous USDA-funded research, finds that current ZEV Class 8 trucks cost 2-3 times more than diesel equivalents ($450,000+ for electric, $550,000+ for hydrogen versus $160,000 for a new diesel), offer limited range (150-160 miles for battery-electric versus 500 miles for hydrogen), and weigh approximately 10,000 pounds more, forcing payload reductions of about 6,000 pounds that could increase product costs by 3-4% or more. Agricultural exporters face disproportionate impacts because they compete in global commodity markets with thin margins where cost increases cannot be easily passed to buyers, operate longer distances between rural processing facilities and ports, and experience seasonal demand peaks. 

Our research and this study recommends agricultural-specific policy frameworks including enhanced weight allowances, rural infrastructure development, and seasonal-use incentives while noting potential long-term competitive advantages as ZEV technology matures and manufacturing costs approach parity with diesel vehicles by 2027-2030.

title: Paraguay as a Late Oligarchy: An Agrarian-Fiscal Order Measured Against Argentina’s Conservative State, 1880–1916

detail.title: Paraguay as a Late Oligarchy: An Agrarian-Fiscal Order Measured Against Argentina’s Conservative State, 1880–1916
detail.abstract: Paraguay cut poverty from 51 to about 20 per cent in two decades and reached an investment-grade rating in 2024 while collecting 14.5 per cent of GDP in tax, one of the three lowest fiscal efforts in Latin America, and holding a land Gini coefficient of 0.93, the highest concentration recorded for any country. This paper reads that coexistence as a single arrangement and calls it a late oligarchy: markets, elections, and macroeconomic management resting on an elite bloc whose grip on land, on the design of taxation, and on the territorial distribution of public goods none of those instruments has loosened. Land concentration, fiscal minimalism, two-thirds informality, out-of-pocket health financing near 36 per cent, maternal mortality among the region's highest, and the long dominance of the Colorado Party belong to one political economy. The comparison with Argentina's conservative order of 1880-1916 fixes the type and reverses on one axis: Argentina restricted the suffrage while building a mass institutional state, Law 1420, railways, immigration, bureaucracy; Paraguay extends electoral citizenship while leaving the social state thin. The Argentine precedent survives in Paraguay on its oligarchic side and not on its state-building side. Falling income inequality and widening targeted transfers are read against this structure: the flow has moved, the stock has not.

title: Pricing Accuracy vs. Trading Profit in Retail Options Trading
affiliations: , Tecnologico de Monterrey, Tecnologico de Monterrey, Tecnologico de Monterrey and Tecnologico de Monterrey

detail.title: Pricing Accuracy vs. Trading Profit in Retail Options Trading
detail.abstract: Machine-learning models for option pricing routinely report substantial root-mean-square-error (RMSE) improvements over closed-form baselines, but it remains unclear whether those improvements translate to trading profit under realistic retail constraints. This paper compares four pricers (Black-Scholes [BS], Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree [BT], XGBoost [XGB], and a Multi-Layer Perceptron [MLP]) on 18.2 million minute-bar S&P 500 call observations spanning a 17month walk-forward out-of-sample window (six quarterly folds). Each model is evaluated on two axes: pricing accuracy by RMSE, and realized trading profit-and-loss through a discrete-event simulator with retail-grade costs ($0.65/contract commission, 5% bid-ask spread). The two axes disagree. The ML methods deliver the lowest aggregate RMSE (MLP 1.96, XGB 1.98 versus BS 2.99, a 34% reduction), while the parametric methods deliver the highest risk-adjusted returns (BT Sharpe 2.11 with six of six positive quarterly folds, versus XGB 0.74 and MLP-0.13). The rank inversion holds across eight simulator configurations spanning stop-loss, take-profit, position cap, and bid-ask variations. The ML failure is attributed to extreme overestimation errors on illiquid contracts that mechanical entry rules cannot distinguish from genuine mispricings. The result implies that retail practitioners should not adopt ML pricers on the basis of RMSE alone, and motivates confidence-aware deployment strategies as the natural next step.

title: Continuity-Constrained Recovery: Adapting Root Cause Analysis and the Critical Path Method in Occupied Facilities

detail.title: Continuity-Constrained Recovery: Adapting Root Cause Analysis and the Critical Path Method in Occupied Facilities
detail.abstract: Operations management's core techniques were largely developed for manufacturing and project environments, yet facilities and service organizations routinely rely on them when responding to operational disruptions. This paper examines how two such techniques, Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and the Critical Path Method (CPM), were applied during the recovery of a multi-site facilities operation following a drainage-system failure triggered by the September 2023 New York City flash flood. Using a de-identified case analyzed through a reflective-practitioner lens, the paper draws on the author's experience leading the recovery effort while maintaining continuity of service in occupied facilities. The case revealed that RCA had to extend beyond the immediate trigger of the disruption to identify a latent vulnerability in the building's infrastructure and that the investigation itself had to be conducted indirectly because service could not be suspended. It also showed that CPM's traditional objective of minimizing downtime shifted toward maintaining operational continuity during recovery activities. Rather than occurring in sequence, diagnosis and recovery planning evolved together as new information emerged and operational decisions were made. These observations form the basis of the Continuity-Constrained Recovery (CCR) model and four propositions for future application and research. The paper contributes a practitioner-centered perspective to the operations and resilience literatures. It offers a practical framework for managers responsible for restoring critical infrastructure while continuing to serve occupants and stakeholders.

title: Nature-positive, Net Zero Land-use Futures Possible for Australia at Feasible Shadow Prices
affiliations: Deakin University - Melbourne Burwood Campus, Deakin University - Melbourne Burwood Campus, Deakin University - Centre for Integrative Ecology, Deakin University, Government of the Commonwealth of Australia - CSIRO Energy, Government of the Commonwealth of Australia - CSIRO Energy, Deakin University and Deakin University - Centre for Integrative Ecology

detail.title: Nature-positive, Net Zero Land-use Futures Possible for Australia at Feasible Shadow Prices
detail.abstract: Achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and ecosystem restoration requires understanding the economic costs of land-sector transitions, yet spatially explicit estimates of carbon and biodiversity shadow prices remain limited. Using the spatiotemporal Land Use Trade-Offs Model version 2 (LUTO2), we simulated stacked climate and biodiversity targets for Australia and quantified the costs and shadow prices associated with achieving them through land-use change and management. Total costs were dominated by transitions from agricultural to non-agricultural land uses. Shadow carbon prices increased from AU$58 tCO₂e⁻¹ yr⁻¹ under net-zero-only targets to AU$132 tCO₂e⁻¹ yr⁻¹ when biodiversity targets were added, while shadow biodiversity prices peaked at AU$846 ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Costs and shadow prices varied across space, providing a spatially explicit basis for targeting carbon and biodiversity investments toward net-zero emissions and Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Target 2 in Australia. The framework can support integrated land-sector planning in other regions pursuing climate and biodiversity targets.

title: Spatiotemporal Burden, Risk Factors, and Genetic Causality of Ischemic Heart Disease and Ischemic Stroke Comorbidity in Asia: A Multi-database Analysis
affiliations: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, Guangxi Medical University - Cancer Hospital, Fuzhou University, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences and China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

detail.title: Spatiotemporal Burden, Risk Factors, and Genetic Causality of Ischemic Heart Disease and Ischemic Stroke Comorbidity in Asia: A Multi-database Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors confirm that there are no conflicts of interest associated with this manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: The study was financially supported by Scientific and Technological Innovation Project of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences（CI2026A00910）.

detail.abstract:
Background: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) and ischemic stroke (IS) are the leading cardiovascular diseases in Asia, though significant variations persist across different countries and regions. Monitoring the burden of IHD and IS across Asian regions holds significant scientific and public health value for optimizing the allocation of healthcare resources and developing targeted prevention and control strategies.

Methods: This study utilized data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study and applied Mendelian randomization (MR) methods to assess trends in age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR), disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) for ischemic heart disease (IHD) and stroke (IS). The analysis was disaggregated by sex, 17 age groups, 5 regions, and 5 Socioeconomic Development Index (SDI) categories, and MR was used to conduct a detailed analysis of the risk factors for both conditions.

Results: The results show that the burden of IHD and IS in Asia remains significant, and both absolute and relative inequalities are increasing across regions, with the burden of both diseases being particularly heavy in regions with medium SDI. Regarding IHD, the ASIR in Central Asia in 2023 was 290.61 (95% UI 256.72–327.89), significantly higher than in other regions. For IS, Southeast Asia had the highest ASIR at 120.85 (95% UI 106.44–137.40), while South Asia exhibited the most pronounced upward trend in EAPC at 0.33 (95% CI 0.18–0.47). Analysis by age and gender revealed that in most Asian regions, older men face significantly elevated risks for both diseases; However, in Central and Southeast Asia, the burden of IS was notably higher among women. Although the burden of both diseases remained consistently low in high-income Asia-Pacific regions, the rate of increase in DALYs and mortality with advancing age among the elderly ranked highest in Asia. Risk factor analysis revealed that from 1990 to 2023, high systolic blood pressure, air pollution, and high and low LDL- C consistently ranked among the top three risk factors. Further meta-regression analysis confirmed that, in addition to the traditionally recognized high systolic blood pressure, high diastolic blood pressure was also significantly associated with both diseases, whereas air pollution did not show statistical significance; further validation is needed in the future.

Conclusion: Although the burden of IHD and stroke has decreased between 1990 and 2023, inequalities persist and have even worsened in some regions; therefore, it is crucial to implement timely and effective disease prevention and management strategies in specific areas.

title: Have Mount Laurel Obligations Made New Jersey Housing More Affordable? A Synthetic Control Analysis of Housing Supply and Cost

detail.title: Have Mount Laurel Obligations Made New Jersey Housing More Affordable? A Synthetic Control Analysis of Housing Supply and Cost
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effect of affordable housing obligations in New Jersey on cost of living, cost of housing, and actual housing production. New Jersey’s Mount Laurel court cases established a doctrine whereby municipalities must permit their “fair share” of affordably priced housing. At various points since then, the legislature has interpreted this doctrine with specific, quantitative targets for municipalities to reach, or it has declined to do so, leaving enforcement up to the courts, which in turn backed away for several years from enforcing affordable housing targets. These policy changes provide an opportunity to investigate whether affordable housing targets are having their intended effect. Based on synthetic control analysis, the results show no effect of affordable housing mandates on housing production and minimal to no effect of affordable housing mandates on housing costs.

title: Does Revenue Back Valuation? Protocol Revenue Multiples and the Cross-Section of Token Returns in Decentralized Finance
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Does Revenue Back Valuation? Protocol Revenue Multiples and the Cross-Section of Token Returns in Decentralized Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is an independent researcher and declares no competing financial or personal interests. The author has no advisory, employment, or equity relationship with any of the protocols analyzed in this study.

detail.abstract:
A recurring narrative in digital-asset markets holds that tokens of protocols with "real revenue" are fundamentally cheaper and should outperform. I test this directly using the full cross-section of fee- and revenue-reporting protocols tracked by DefiLlama (2,259 protocols; 345 with a traded market capitalization) and one year of daily price and market-capitalization data. Three findings emerge. First, valuation is economically disconnected from revenue at the level of the market: a single asset (Bitcoin) accounts for 90.5% of sample market capitalization, tokens with essentially no measurable protocol revenue represent roughly 92% of market capitalization, and even among application protocols revenue multiples are extraordinarily dispersed (median price-to-revenue of 9.0× spanning well below 1× to effectively unbounded). Second, in the cross-section of forward returns, the formation-date revenue multiple has no power to discriminate winners from losers: over a window in which the median token fell 78.7% and only 5.3% of tokens posted a positive return, the rank correlation between price-to-revenue and the subsequent twelve-month return is statistically zero (Spearman ρ = 0.04), and is unchanged after controlling for size and asset class (slope on log price-to-revenue = -0.0004, p = 0.98). Third, in a monthly Fama-MacBeth panel the relationship is, if anything, weakly anti-value (mean ρ = +0.063, t = 2.18): cheaper-on-revenue tokens did marginally worse, not better. The evidence does not support a revenue-based value premium in this market and period; the dominant force in returns was a near-uniform sector-wide repricing. Results are specific to a single, predominantly bearish regime and to a universe conditioned on revenue generation, limitations I discuss in detail.

detail.abstract: Frameworks for AI accountability consistently locate failure in static gaps: the responsibility gap, the liability gap, the accountability gap, the problem of many hands, the moral crumple zone, and Santoni de Sio and Mecacci's recent four-part elaboration of the responsibility gap. The lifecycle approaches now emerging in policy literature extend the temporal scope of governance by multiplying the moments at which accountability can be assessed, but they retain the same structural premise. All of these framings share an assumption so deep in the literature it has become invisible: accountability failure can be located at a place in the deployment chain.

title: Financial Constraints and Optimal Regulatory Disclosures
affiliations: Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto

detail.title: Financial Constraints and Optimal Regulatory Disclosures
detail.abstract: How much information about financial institutions' balance sheets should regulators disclose to the market? Financial constraints generate a direct preference for transparency. Further, they induce strategic complementarities among investors: Weak fundamentals increase the fear of miscoordination, leading to haircuts and underprovision of capital. As liquidity constraints relax, the coordination friction fades and funding liquidity is restored. In response, the optimal policy imposes transparency for weak fundamentals and opacity, otherwise. Transparency increases with the deterioration of the assets and liquidity buffers, and with more stringent financial constraints. This simple policy is robust to investors' adversarial coordination and the firm's strategic reaction.

title: The Trinity of State Decay (Part 1): Sovereign Decoupling and Rival Sovereignty — A Theoretical Statement

detail.title: The Trinity of State Decay (Part 1): Sovereign Decoupling and Rival Sovereignty — A Theoretical Statement
detail.abstract: The Trinity of State Decay (TSD) advances a theoretical claim: state decay in the Global South is not institutional malfunction but a sovereignty eventthe structural decoupling of juridical statehood from empirical authority into rival orders. This departs from failed state theory, hybrid governance, and fragility frameworks, which operate at the national aggregate and cannot explain the coexistence of functional and decoupled sovereignty within the same juridical unit. TSD identifies two formations: the Institutional Mirage, which performs authority without possessing it, and the Shadow Order, which governs without formal legitimacy. Their interaction is sustained by the Money-Land-Mind dynamic, displacing financial, territorial, and normative authority from the state to rival structures. Decay is zonal before national, partial before total. Recovery requires strict sequencing: protection before compliance, compliance before territorial credibility, and credibility before institutional function; inversion produces relapse. Drawing on African political thought, postcolonial theory, classical political theory, and comparative politics, TSD offers a generalisable framework for analysing sovereign fragmentation. Its empirical operationalisationincluding quantitative measurement of decoupling depth and recovery sequencingis developed in the companion Decoupling Sovereignty Index (DSI), Part 2 of this series.

title: Transferring Return Predictability to the Beijing Stock Exchange
affiliations: and East China Normal University (ECNU)

detail.title: Transferring Return Predictability to the Beijing Stock Exchange
detail.abstract: We investigate whether stock return predictability on the Beijing Stock Exchange (BSE), a young market with limited historical data, can be improved by transferring information from the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE). Models that incorporate source-market information substantially outperform a BSE-only benchmark, with the monthly out-of-sample R-squared increasing from 0.36% to 1.53% and the annualized Sharpe ratio of long-short portfolios rising from 1.31 to 3.80. A prediction-correlation analysis further indicates a strong China-wide component, with a prediction-based China-wide importance measure of 99.99%. Our findings provide early and suggestive evidence that cross-market transfer learning can help address data scarcity in emerging equity markets.

title: How Can Intraday Variance Concentration Signal Next-Day Crash Risk? Evidence from S&P 500 High-Frequency Data
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: How Can Intraday Variance Concentration Signal Next-Day Crash Risk? Evidence from S&P 500 High-Frequency Data

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Derivatives and Quantitative Studies, Forthcoming

detail.abstract:
Purpose: This paper examines whether the temporal distribution of intraday realized variance forecasts next-day equity crash risk beyond the level of realized variance alone. 

Design/methodology/approach: Using 3,867 days of five-minute S&P 500 data (2005-2020) spanning the 2008 financial crisis and 2020 COVID-19 crash, the authors introduce the Herfindahl Index of Intraday Variance (HHI t), prove a level-independent diffusion baseline, and evaluate HHI t in an expanding-window out-of-sample logistic framework against nine benchmarks, including GARCH(1,1), HAR-RV, and a realized-variance random walk. Forecast quality is assessed via ROC-AUC, Brier score, calibration analysis, and Diebold-Mariano tests. 

Findings: Under pure diffusion, E[HHI t ] = 3n/(n+2) is independent of the volatility level, confirmed empirically (correlation:-0.11). Conditional on realized variance, HHI t carries a significant negative coefficient (p = 0.022): broad-based variance days precede crashes more reliably than isolated-burst days of equal total variance. The proposed model achieves the lowest out-of-sample Brier score of all ten specifications and exposes a 100-fold GARCH calibration failure in low-risk environments. A cash-overlay strategy raises the Sharpe ratio from 0.25 to 0.58. 

Originality: This paper provides the first formally proved level-independent baseline for an intraday variance concentration measure and the first systematic out-of-sample comparison of such a measure against established crash-forecasting benchmarks.

title: The Role of Ecosystem Services in Supporting Rural Livelihoods around Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria
affiliations: Federal University of Technology, Akure and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Role of Ecosystem Services in Supporting Rural Livelihoods around Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria
detail.abstract: Ecosystem services play a critical role in supporting rural livelihoods, particularly in communities located around protected areas where dependence on natural resources remains high. This study examined the contribution of ecosystem services to rural livelihood sustainability in communities adjoining Old Oyo National Park, Nigeria. Specifically, the study identified key ecosystem resources utilized by local communities and assessed their importance in supporting household livelihoods and socioeconomic well-being. Primary data were collected through the administration of 384 structured questionnaires among residents of selected support-zone communities surrounding the park using a multistage sampling technique. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods. The findings revealed that respondents derived significant livelihood benefits from ecosystem services provided by the park. Major ecosystem resources identified included fauna resources (80.7%), flora resources (78.6%), fertile land (76.3%), medicinal plants (70.1%), clean water (59.6%), grassland resources (59.9%), and cultural relics (54.4%). Respondents further considered bush meat, bush food, medicinal plants, water resources, and hunting activities as highly important for household sustenance and income generation. The results demonstrate the strong dependence of rural households on ecosystem services for food security, healthcare, employment, and environmental sustainability. The study concludes that ecosystem services provided by Old Oyo National Park contribute significantly to rural livelihood resilience and community welfare. Consequently, conservation policies should 2 integrate biodiversity protection with livelihood improvement strategies to ensure sustainable resource management and long-term ecosystem sustainability.
